title: AI detects Parkinson's disease from nocturnal breathing signals
summary: An attention-based AI model extracting breathing from radio waves during sleep detected Parkinson's disease with an AUC of 0.90 on held-out data and 0.85 on external sets, across 7,671 individuals. Its severity estimates correlated with MDS-UPDRS scores (R = 0.94), and it worked for at-home assessment. Caveat: largely retrospective data and no prospective diagnostic trial reported.
ai_technology: Attention-based deep learning on contactless radio-wave breathing signals
organization: Mayo Clinic; University of Rochester Medical Center; Massachusetts Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Parkinson's detection was tested on held-out data (AUC 0.90) and external test sets (AUC 0.85) across 7,671 individuals, and severity estimates were compared with MDS-UPDRS scores (R = 0.94).
evidence.unknown: The authors describe the findings as initial evidence that the model may be useful for risk assessment before clinical diagnosis.
evidence.ai_role: Attention-based AI model extracting breathing from radio waves during sleep to detect and grade Parkinson's disease.
